correctness.rationale: Derive products by direct summation: X*Y=r(X)c(Y)^t. The row/column sum map onto the common-total hyperplane has dimension m+n-1 and fiber size q^((m-1)(n-1)). Compute the four centralizer subspace dimensions m+n-1,n-1,m-1,1; their populations partition q^(m+n-1). Rank two holds iff both the row and column 2-frames have full rank, whose counts with coordinate-sum vector zero/nonzero yield F_d^(0),F_d^(*). Subtract rank-zero and rank-two counts from q^(2mn) for rank one. All edge cases m or n=1 are included and the rank-two geometric statement has an explicit independent-frame witness. Direct coefficient multiplication and Gaussian elimination produced the exact predicted three-rank histogram in eight exhaustive tests including GF4.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text operator-band paper proves a cubic relation for commutators of individual operator-band members but neither enumerates commutators of arbitrary elements of an F_q-semigroup algebra nor studies coefficient-array rank. The full accessible band-cohomology article investigates cyclic/simplicial groups instead. The matrix-semigroup commutable-rank article compares ranks of products rather than differences, according to its accessible abstract. A later Rees matrix semigroup commuting-graph theorem counts semigroup vertices, not linear combinations. Exact claim/alias searches surfaced different algebra commutator censuses, e.g. finite Kronecker path algebras, but no dominating rectangular-band coefficient-rank count. Residual risk: uncatalogued semigroup-ring enumerations or implicit extensions from historical literature.

value.rationale: The exact three-rank distribution, four element-centralizer strata and generic rank threshold are natural Lie statistics of a finite associative algebra, and are uniform in arbitrary finite field and both unbounded band parameters. The contrast between a basis semigroup in which distinct elements never commute and its linear span, in which large families of elements commute, is mathematically motivated. The census is neither a single small case nor a restatement of a nilpotent-element count; it separates rank-zero, rank-one and generically rank-two phenomena.
